# blng sprint

> Fixed-price, architect-led sprints from blng studio, a principal-led architecture practice in London, UK. A sprint is a short, fixed-price piece of architect-led work with a defined scope and set deliverables, aimed at one decision about a building, site, team or career. We work on sites in the UK; prices and invoices are in GBP.

Each sprint's scope and fixed price are confirmed in a written proposal before you commit. Most of our sprints are for businesses and organisations. The Portfolio Review Sprint is for individuals: graduates, Part 1 and Part 2 students and early-career architects. We don't currently offer sprints for homeowners.

## Sprints

- [Nursery & School Premises Sprint](https://sprint.blng.studio/sprints/nursery-school-premises-sprint/): from £1,950 + VAT. Will this building work as a nursery or school, before you sign the lease? For: Nursery and school founders, nursery groups and schools adding a nursery. England only.
- [Workspace Brief Sprint](https://sprint.blng.studio/sprints/workspace-brief-sprint/): from £2,450 + VAT. What office do we need, and what will the fit-out cost, before we talk to fit-out contractors? For: Startups and growing companies taking, moving or reconfiguring an office.
- [Feasibility Sprint](https://sprint.blng.studio/sprints/feasibility-sprint/): Fixed fee, quoted per site after a free intro call. What can this site hold, and how do the options compare, before you commit? For: Small developers, landowners and investors testing what a site can hold.
- [Portfolio Review Sprint](https://sprint.blng.studio/sprints/portfolio-review-sprint/): £70 incl. VAT. Is your portfolio ready to get you the interview, before you apply? For: Graduates, Part 1 and Part 2 students and early-career architects applying for jobs.

## Guides

- [Job Search Launchpad](https://sprint.blng.studio/sprints/job-search-launchpad/): £24 incl. VAT, PDF workbook. Not sure where to start your job search? A short, AI-guided workbook to take stock before you apply. For: Graduates, Part 1 and Part 2 students and early-career architects starting a job search.

## Free resources

- [Will this building work? The free premises checklist for nursery founders](https://sprint.blng.studio/free-resources/nursery-school/): Free · for nursery founders · England. Premises checklist (PDF); EYFS capacity calculator (Excel spreadsheet).
- [Before you send it: the free portfolio self-check](https://sprint.blng.studio/free-resources/portfolio-self-check/): Free · for graduates, students and early-career architects. Portfolio self-check: 16 yes/no questions (PDF, one page).
- [Before you sign: the office floor scorecard](https://sprint.blng.studio/free-resources/office-floor-scorecard/): Free · for teams of about 10 to 100 · England. Office floor scorecard (PDF, two pages); Scorecard spreadsheet (Excel spreadsheet).
- [Site first look: the one-hour desktop check before you offer](https://sprint.blng.studio/free-resources/site-first-look/): Free · for landowners, developers and investors · England. Site first look: a one-hour desktop check (PDF, two pages).

## Articles

- [Nursery space requirements: how much space per child?](https://sprint.blng.studio/articles/nursery-space-requirements/): How much space per child a nursery needs under the EYFS, what counts as usable space and how to test a building's capacity.
- [What use class is a nursery? Planning permission explained](https://sprint.blng.studio/articles/nursery-planning-permission-use-class/): Day nurseries are Class E(f): when you need planning permission, what an office-to-nursery move involves and the traps to check first.
- [Will this building work for a nursery? Check before you sign](https://sprint.blng.studio/articles/will-this-building-work-for-a-nursery/): What to test before you sign a nursery lease: space, planning, Ofsted readiness, toilets, outdoor play and escape routes.
- [Opening a second nursery site: what to check first](https://sprint.blng.studio/articles/opening-a-second-nursery/): Ofsted approves each nursery setting separately. What to check first: expansion or new setting, a manager for the site, and the premises themselves.
- [Ofsted registration for a new nursery: timeline and visit](https://sprint.blng.studio/articles/ofsted-registration-for-a-nursery/): What GOV.UK says about how long nursery registration takes, the steps and the fee, and why the premises must be ready before Ofsted visits.
- [How much office space does a startup really need?](https://sprint.blng.studio/articles/how-much-office-space-do-i-need/): Work out your office size from peak attendance, not headcount: desks, meeting rooms and support space, with the UK benchmarks behind them.
- [What to check before signing a lease for your first office](https://sprint.blng.studio/articles/office-lease-checklist/): Use class, EPC, the 1954 Act, break clauses, repair and dilapidations, service charge and your fit-out: what to check, and when, before you sign.
- [Writing a workspace brief before you talk to agents or fit-out contractors](https://sprint.blng.studio/articles/office-fit-out-brief/): The six parts of an office brief, and how one document keeps agents, landlords and fit-out contractors answering the same question.
- [Cat A vs Cat B fit-out: what the landlord hands over, and what you add](https://sprint.blng.studio/articles/cat-a-vs-cat-b-fit-out/): Shell and core, Cat A, Cat A+ and Cat B in plain terms: who usually provides what, and what to pin down in heads of terms before you sign.
- [What is a test-fit, and when do you need one?](https://sprint.blng.studio/articles/office-test-fit/): What a test-fit shows on a floor you're considering, the questions it answers, when to get one before heads of terms, and what it doesn't do.
- [How many homes can I build on my land?](https://sprint.blng.studio/articles/how-many-homes-can-i-build-on-my-land/): A first look at what sets a site's capacity in England, from planning policy and constraints to space standards and fire rules, before you buy.
- [What a feasibility study tells you (and what it doesn't)](https://sprint.blng.studio/articles/what-a-feasibility-study-tells-you/): What an architect's feasibility study covers, what it leaves to planners, surveyors and solicitors, and where it sits before pre-app and planning.
- [Office to flats without planning permission: Class MA](https://sprint.blng.studio/articles/office-to-residential-class-ma/): When an office can become homes under Class MA in England: the conditions, what the council checks at prior approval, and the space and light tests.
- [Architecture portfolio tips: what practices look at in the first minute](https://sprint.blng.studio/articles/architecture-portfolio-tips/): What a reviewer takes in from your portfolio in the first minute, how to choose and order projects, show your role, and send the PDF.
- [How to structure an architecture portfolio](https://sprint.blng.studio/articles/how-to-structure-an-architecture-portfolio/): The order of pages in a portfolio for a job application, a simple template for each project, and a way to restructure the one you have.
- [Part 1 vs Part 2 portfolio: what changes](https://sprint.blng.studio/articles/part-1-vs-part-2-architecture-portfolio/): What a practice looks for in a Part 1 architectural assistant portfolio and in a Part 2 one, and how the order and content shift between them.
